newsitem.title: ERITREA: Eritrean development bank to open next year.
newsitem.headline: Eritrean development bank to open next year.

text.p: The newly established Eritrean Development and Investment Bank will be fully operational within a few months, the general manager said on Thursday.

The bank, with initial capital of 45 million birr ($7 million) provided by the government, will be the main local source of long-term finance in the new state, which won independence from Ethiopia in 1993.

"The proclamation to establish this bank was published on October 28. We are not operational yet, but we will be in four or five months. We expect to start work in the second quarter of 1997," manager Ahmed Sayed Ali told Reuters in an interview.

"This country does not have a financial institution which can give long-term credits and loans. This is the main financial institution which will handle long-term loans for development purposes," he added. "It will give loans for projects in agriculture, industry...tourism and fisheries."
Ahmed Sayed Ali said the 45 million birr would not be enough and the bank would borrow from domestic and international institutions, including the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
"With this capital as the base I think we can raise four times as much through loans and through agreements with governments," he said.

"The government obtains financial assistance from other governments and this bank will serve the purpose of handling that money. The government cannot do it itself, so they will channel the money through us," he added.
